user.title: Connect to the boiler
user.description: Enter the address of your Hargassner boiler. Its touch control must be connected to your network by cable; the display shows the IP address in the network settings. The integration only reads values, it never changes anything on the boiler.

data_description.name: Becomes the name of the device in Home Assistant.
data_description.port: The boiler listens on port 23. Only change this if you forward the port yourself.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Change the address of the boiler. The data format is detected again afterwards, which is also what you need after a firmware update.

layout.title: Select the data format
layout.description:
The boiler sends {count} values per line. More than one known firmware layout has this length, or none of them matches exactly. Select the layout of your boiler; the next step shows the result so you can check it.

Layouts marked with (?) do not match the number format of the received line and are probably wrong.

custom.title: Use the boiler's own description
custom.description:
The boiler sends {count} values per line. To tell the integration what they mean, you can use the description the boiler writes itself:

1. Enable logging to the SD card on the touch display and insert an SD card for a few minutes.
2. Open the file `{file}` from the card in a text editor.
3. Near the top there is a block that starts with `{tag_open}` and ends with `{tag_close}`. Copy the whole block and paste it below.

confirm.title: Do these values look right?
confirm.description:
Layout: **{layout}**

Values read from the boiler just now:

{preview}

Compare them with the display of the boiler. If they are plausible, finish the setup. If they are clearly wrong, this layout does not belong to your firmware.

error.cannot_connect: No connection. Check the address and that the boiler is switched on and reachable in your network.
error.no_telegram: The device answers, but does not send Hargassner data. Check the address and the port.
error.invalid_daqprj: This is not a usable DAQPRJ block. Copy everything from the opening to the closing DAQPRJ tag.
error.count_mismatch: The block describes a different number of values than the boiler sends ({count}). It probably comes from another firmware version.

abort.already_configured: This boiler is already set up.

data.pellet_energy: Energy content of the pellets (kWh per kg)
data.raw_channels: Create entities for all other channels

data_description.scan_interval: How often the values are read from the boiler.
data_description.pellet_energy: Used for the pellet energy sensor. Changing it only affects pellets burnt from now on.
data_description.raw_channels: Adds every remaining value and status bit of the boiler as a disabled diagnostic entity, named as the boiler names it. Enable the ones you need.

layout_mismatch.title: The boiler {name} sends a different data format
layout_mismatch.description:
The boiler now sends {received} values per line, but the configured layout has {expected}. This usually happens after a firmware update. Until the layout is corrected, the entities are unavailable rather than showing wrong values.

Open the integration, choose Reconfigure from the menu of the entry and confirm the address; the layout is then detected again.
